name: Walking Stick
description:
A straight, seasoned ash stick about five feet long, smoothed at the grip and capped at the foot with a plain iron ferrule. It offers a steady handhold on uneven ground and can probe shallow mud or undergrowth.

This entry is ordinary travelling gear, without an automatic movement bonus or weapon attack. Any improvised use is resolved by the GM.

weight.notes: One pound for a slim seasoned wooden stick and small protective ferrule.

name: Compass
description:
A balanced magnetic needle turns beneath a simple marked dial in a hinged brass case. In ordinary conditions it indicates magnetic north, giving a traveller a useful reference for orientation.

This specialist project item does not reveal a destination, draw a map or replace navigation checks. Local magnetic interference, unusual environments and magical effects are adjudicated by the GM. No automatic Survival bonus is applied.
saleUnit: One pocket magnetic compass in a brass case

weight.notes: One tenth of a pound for a small needle assembly, dial and protective brass case.

name: Spyglass
description:
A compact brass viewing tube with fitted glass lenses and a sliding focus. Looking through it makes distant objects appear twice as large, following the 2014 equipment rule.

The spyglass needs a clear line of sight and suitable light. It grants no darkvision, ability to see invisible creatures or automatic Perception bonus. Its price is a deliberate project adjustment for a specialist village-order purchase.

weight.notes: Three quarters of a pound for a compact brass tube and lenses, adjusted from heavier full-sized optics.

source.title: Devil's Table: Goods & Provisions
source.reference: 2014 SRD 5.1 equipment: a spyglass doubles apparent object size. Project price is 100 gp, rather than the SRD's 1,000 gp. Original wording; project prices and adjusted weights. See docs/GENERAL_STORE_REVIEW.md.

name: Bell
description:
A small brass bell with a metal clapper and a loop for holding or tying to a cord. Its clear ring suits calling attention, marking a routine signal or sounding when an attached line is disturbed.

Cord and any alarm rigging are separate. How far it can be heard depends on background noise, obstructions and circumstances; the item applies no automatic detection or alarm effect.

weight.notes: One tenth of a pound for the bell, clapper and attachment loop.

name: Signal Whistle
description:
A small wooden whistle pierced for a carrying cord. A sharp breath produces a high, clear note useful for agreed signals between travellers or workers.

No cord is included. Companions must agree what a signal means, and the GM determines whether it can be heard through distance, weather and surrounding noise. It has no fixed detection radius or magical effect.

weight.notes: Two hundredths of a pound for a single small wooden whistle.

name: Steel Mirror
description:
A palm-sized polished steel face gives a serviceable reflection without a glass pane. Its plain backing has a small grip, and an included cloth sleeve protects the polished surface.

Ordinary scratches and dirt reduce clarity. It is a reflective tool, with no divination, detection or automatic signalling range.
saleUnit: One polished steel hand mirror with cloth sleeve

weight.notes: One fifth of a pound for the small mirror and protective sleeve.

name: Hourglass
description:
Two joined glass bulbs sit within a small wooden frame. When upright and undisturbed, their measured dry sand takes about one hour to pass through the neck.

Movement, tilt and damp can disturb the result. The timer neither tracks calendar time nor pauses spell durations; it is an ordinary approximate measure.

weight.notes: Half a pound for the glass, sand and protective frame.

name: Road Map
description:
A copied paper map marks the principal roads, settlements and crossings in one district named at purchase. A merchant or the GM identifies the covered area before the sheet is useful in play.

No world map is generated automatically. The map may omit recent changes, hidden routes and hazards, and its presence does not replace navigation checks.
saleUnit: One paper route map for a named local district

weight.notes: Two hundredths of a pound for a single folded route sheet.

source.title: Devil's Table: Goods & Provisions

name: Waterproof Document Wrap
description:
A waxed cloth square folds around a few flat papers and ties shut with an attached cord. Overlapping folds protect against ordinary rain and splashes when packed carefully.

Documents are separate. Despite its trade name, the wrap is not an immersion-proof seal; track enclosed sheets separately and do not treat it as weightless storage.
saleUnit: One waxed cloth wrap for folded documents

weight.notes: One tenth of a pound for the empty treated cloth and attached tie.

name: Travel Cloak
description:
A plain hooded wool cloak closes with a wooden toggle and hangs over ordinary clothes. Its dense weave reduces wind and sheds light rain for a time.

It is travel clothing, not armour or equipment for extreme cold. It grants no resistance, stealth bonus or automatic protection from exposure.
saleUnit: One hooded wool travel cloak sized for one Medium wearer

weight.notes: Two pounds for the complete single-person wool cloak and fastening.

name: Pack Cover
description:
An oiled canvas hood fits over an ordinary backpack and tightens with a sewn-in draw cord. It protects the pack's exposed upper surface from ordinary rain and road dirt.

The backpack is separate. A cover is not a sealed flotation bag and does not enlarge carrying capacity or protect against immersion.
saleUnit: One draw-cord oiled canvas cover for a backpack

weight.notes: Thirty-five hundredths of a pound for the cover and draw cord, without a pack.

source.title: Devil's Table: Goods & Provisions

name: Canvas Repair Patches
description:
Four hemmed squares of waxed canvas patch small worn areas in a groundsheet, tent or pack. Their prepared edges make them convenient to stitch over sound surrounding material.

A needle, thread and any sealing wax are separate. A patch requires ordinary repair work and cannot automatically restore a destroyed shelter or grant weather immunity.
saleUnit: One packet of four waxed canvas patches, six inches square

weight.notes: Fifteen hundredths of a pound for four prepared cloth patches and their paper wrap.

name: Marking Ribbon
description:
A narrow roll of plainly dyed cloth can be cut into markers for a trail, baggage or agreed camp signals. Its colour is chosen from the merchant's ordinary stock.

Markers can be moved, hidden or weathered away. Ribbon provides no automatic tracking result and is too light for load-bearing work.
saleUnit: One ten-yard roll of plain coloured cloth ribbon

weight.notes: Five hundredths of a pound for ten yards of thin ribbon and its small winding card.
